ordinary: Lane A: use ordinary outcome-and-constraint analysis to generate up to two useful alternative mechanisms, hypotheses or discriminating questions.
creative: Lane A: use ordinary outcome-and-constraint analysis to generate up to two useful alternative mechanisms, hypotheses or discriminating questions. Deliberately seek unusual, surprising, useful possibilities while preserving the shared commitments.
N01: Lane A: Who or what else could perform the essential function? Move the function into the material, interface, artifact, or environment; name the replacement causal path. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N02: Lane A: Which demand is being generated by the way our solution organizes the world? Add a hypothesized feedback edge from the intervention to demand; derive a counterfactual observation. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N03: Lane A: What relationship could change so the named task no longer has to happen? Remove a dependency by redesigning an interface, then enumerate the obligations formerly satisfied by that dependency. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N04: Lane A: Can the force that defeats the idea become information, energy, or control? Design a conversion from the adverse input to a contribution to the desired function; specify its failure boundary. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N05: Lane A: If this dependency disappeared, what arrangement could still work? Forbid one changeable dependency in a counterfactual branch; generate an alternative and list every replacement dependency. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N06: Lane A: What appears when we study a relation, trajectory, or subclaim rather than the current object? Change one representational dimension and translate back to concrete actions with a recomposition rule. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N07: Lane A: Which unlike system has a relationship we could adapt? Map a source mechanism to the target, including an explicit failed correspondence and changed material assumptions. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N08: Lane A: What could two partial solutions do together that neither can do alone? Cross two mechanisms at a named interface and predict an interaction benefit. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N09: Lane A: What existing property, trace, or by-product could do another job? Bind one available property to a new operation and verify provenance before claiming it is available. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N10: Lane A: What would the provider invent if paid for the maintained outcome? Change a proposed incentive in a model; derive the resulting choices and possible gaming. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N11: Lane A: Which awkward case could teach us a different mechanism? Preserve a sourced anomaly; generate competing mechanisms that explain both ordinary and anomalous cases. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
N12: Lane A: What capabilities would make this surprising object possible? Describe one concrete speculative capability, expand its dependencies, then extract a presently testable partial capability. Generate up to two substantive alternatives or discriminating questions.
